title: Katamari Forever
subtitle: Roll the colour back into memory
summary: Katamari Forever is Genki's PlayStation 3 entry in the rolling action-puzzle series, released in Japan on 23 July 2009. The King of All Cosmos has lost his memory, while the Prince and his cousins have created a troublesome robotic substitute. Part of the adventure takes place inside the King's mind, where gathering objects restores colour to black-and-white scenes. Other assignments ask for new stars after RoboKing's mistakes. The familiar act of growing an adhesive ball now connects two problems: recovering a person's memories and repairing the sky.
body: Katamari Forever is Genki's PlayStation 3 entry in the rolling action-puzzle series, released in Japan on 23 July 2009. The King of All Cosmos has lost his memory, while the Prince and his cousins have created a troublesome robotic substitute. Part of the adventure takes place inside the King's mind, where gathering objects restores colour to black-and-white scenes. Other assignments ask for new stars after RoboKing's mistakes. The familiar act of growing an adhesive ball now connects two problems: recovering a person's memories and repairing the sky.

Most of the game's thirty-four stages draw on earlier Katamari adventures, with a small number of new settings. Returning routes acquire a different role through their presentation and objectives, inviting players to recognise the surroundings while finding another way through them. Size still decides which objects can be collected. A space that first requires careful movement between chairs and shelves can later become something the whole ball overwhelms. The changing scale remains the source of both the route's practical choices and its escalating visual joke.

The Prince Hop lets the katamari leave the ground, adding a way to clear a small obstacle or reach an awkward object. King Shock briefly pulls nearby items toward the ball, giving another means of gathering a dense cluster. Different visual treatments and rearranged music reinforce the game's role as a return through the series. Local multiplayer adds a shared or competitive version of the rolling. Its Japanese title, Katamari Damacy Tribute, expresses that retrospective character particularly clearly: it revisits familiar spaces while giving them a new frame.
